info.name: harrier_api
info.description:
Microsoft Harrier OSS v1 embeddings served by harrier_api — every endpoint, task, model-name form and error case. Mirrors examples/http/*.http.

Start a server first, e.g. `HARRIER_MODELS=270m,0.6b target/release/harrier_api` (port 3000) or `docker compose up -d` (8-bit GGUF on port 13265), pick the matching environment, then run the collection top to bottom: **Health → Models** records the default model's dimensions, **Embeddings** checks vector count, size and normalisation on every request, and the model-card example verifies the published scores.

The `Model names` folder and the by-id/alias model requests assume the 270m is loaded too.

request.description: Liveness / readiness: status, version, uptime, loaded models, compiled backends. Also records the default model and its dimensions for the other requests' tests.
`GET /` returns the health document too.

GAISe-shaped model records: id, provider (`harrier`), display_name, status, capabilities, limits, plus an `embedding` profile (dimension_rule: fixed, task_control, resolved task_instructions) and `runtime` facts (architecture, source, device, dtype, quantization, dequantized, load_seconds, default). The test stores the `{{model}}` record's dimensions as `dims` for the embeddings tests.

exec: const m = ms.find(x => x.id.replace(/^.*::/, "") === want) || ms[0];
console.log("model", m.id, "runs on", m.runtime.device, m.runtime.quantization || m.runtime.dtype, "→", m.limits.embedding_dimensions, "dims");

item.name: Embeddings
item.description: POST /v1/embeddings — the GAISe `GaiseEmbeddingsRequest` contract. Response: `{ output: [[f32; dims], …], usage: { input: { prompt_tokens }, total: { total_tokens } } }`. Vectors come back in input order, unit-length unless `normalize: false`. 270m → 640 dims, 0.6b → 1024 dims.

request.description: Documents are embedded bare (no instruction). Dot product of queries × documents reproduces the model card's `[[66.27, 28.46], [29.77, 69.94]]` (×100) on the 0.6b; the test checks it within ±1.5 (bf16 / int8 drift) when `{{model}}` is the 0.6b.

exec: pm.test("2 vector(s) in input order", () => pm.expect(r.output).to.have.length(2));
const n = Math.sqrt(v.reduce((a, x) => a + x * x, 0));
const dot = (a, b) => a.reduce((s, x, i) => s + x * b[i], 0) * 100;
const scores = q.map(qv => d.map(dv => dot(qv, dv)));
for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) for (let j = 0; j < 2; j++) pm.expect(Math.abs(scores[i][j] - want[i][j])).to.be.below(1.5);

request.description: Symmetric: the instruction `Retrieve semantically similar text` goes on every input.

exec: pm.test("3 vector(s) in input order", () => pm.expect(r.output).to.have.length(3));

pm.test("paraphrases score higher than the unrelated sentence", () => pm.expect(dot(a, b)).to.be.above(dot(a, c)));
